messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT CREATED • P99 INFERENCE TAIL LATENCY spike detected in #inference-prod — automated alert at 2026-03-15T09:02:01Z. Symptoms: streaming stalls (token gaps ~1-3s), p95 ~ 400ms -> 1.8s, p99 ~ 900ms -> 8s. Paging oncall. @sarah (severity: SEV2)

sarah (oncall): I'm on it. Joining from mobile, will jump on the triage call in 2m. @raj can you grab logs/kibana on control-plane/auth path?

raj (sre): On it. Quick look: increase in 429/503 from auth-config-service -> config-store. Early signs: config fetches are being rate-limited, which cascades into inference path since we validate feature flags/config on session start. Running a quick Kibana query: `status:429 AND service:auth-config-service AND @timestamp:[now-10m TO now]`.

alex (eng-runtime): Adding data: runtime traces show many inference requests blocking on `ConfigFetcher.get()` before generation starts. Sampling trace: `inference->auth-check->configfetch (429) -> wait/backoff`. Also seeing repeated retry storms with backoff windows aligning with token floods.

cleo (product): Any customer impact? Are paid customers seeing failures or just latency?

raj (sre): Early metric: ~12% of streaming sessions had stall >1s, 3 customer-facing errors (timeouts) in last 10m. Not widespread but hitting SLOs (p99 breach).

alex (eng-runtime): Paste of log tail (redacted):
```
2026-03-15T09:02:14Z ERROR configfetcher auth-config-service/1 zy: 429 TooManyRequests for /v1/configs?env=prod&service=inference runtime=livestream
2026-03-15T09:02:18Z WARN  inference/runtime request-id=xx latency_wait_ms=1200 blocked_on=configfetch
2026-03-15T09:02:20Z ERROR auth-config-service dbclient: GET configs failed sql.ErrTimeout, retrying
```

raj (sre): DB read p99 for configstore jumped to ~1.2s, queue depth on replica reads spiked. I suspect a hotkey or sudden fanout from a feature-flag change. Checking feature-flag audit now.

sarah (oncall): Ok immediate mitigations: 1) Enable configfetch cache fallback for inference path (serve last-known config) 2) Temporarily reduce configfetch concurrency from runtime (cap = 4) 3) Scale up auth-config-service replicas + add read-only replica for configstore. Who can execute 1 & 2 quickly?

alex (eng-runtime): I can flip the cache fallback flag in the runtime configmap. Command I'll use: `kubectl set env deployment/inference-runtime CONFIG_FETCH_STRATEGY=fallback-cache --namespace=prod` — will push a rolling restart. If we need zero-restart, I can change in-memory toggle via admin endpoint `/admin/flags` (hot). Which do we prefer?

raj (sre): Scaling DB replicas needs infra approval but I can scale auth-config-service now: `kubectl scale deploy auth-config-service --replicas=6 -n prod`. Doing that.

deploy-bot: deploy started: rollout auth-config-service/v2 -> 6 replicas by raj at 2026-03-15T09:04:40Z.

alex (eng-runtime): Hitting admin endpoint now to enable fallback-cache to avoid restart: `curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" https://runtime-admin.prod.internal/admin/flags -d '{"CONFIG_FETCH_STRATEGY":"fallback-cache"}'` — response 200. Enabling.

raj (sre): auth-config-service pods increased, new pods becoming ready. Observability: request 429s are dropping off from ~40/s -> ~7/s in last 90s. DB read latency p99 decreasing to ~350ms.

cleo (product): Good. Any residual customer-facing issues we should notify on status page?

sarah (oncall): We should do a brief status update: "We experienced increased tail latency affecting streaming responses due to cascading config-service rate-limits; mitigations in progress and customer impact limited. Follow-up postmortem planned." I'll draft.

raj (sre): Small follow-up: found a recent rollout of feature-flag `enable_experimental_reranking` which triggered heavy config-fanout to all active sessions ~09:00 UTC. Looks like it caused a hotkey on config keys that aren't cached. Logging snippet: `featureflag-service: broadcast change key=enable_experimental_reranking targets=global` — observers: spike aligns.

alex (eng-runtime): Timeline summary for handoff: root cause (probable) = feature-flag broadcast causing configfetch hot fanout -> auth-config-service rate-limit -> configstore read queue -> inference runtime blocked waiting on config. Mitigations applied: runtime fallback-cache enabled, auth-config-service scaled to 6 replicas, temporary concurrency cap applied client-side. Current status: p99 trending back to normal (now ~420ms), streaming stalls reduced.

ingrid (oncall): Taking over handoff from sarah. I'll keep the incident open for another 90m and collect metrics for postmortem. Action items I have: 1) confirm feature-flag rollback / rate-limit window with product 2) request DB read replica warmup and query hotspot analysis 3) add server-side circuit-breaker for configfetch to prevent retry storms.

sarah (oncall): Thanks. Quick notes for handoff: severity SEV2; customer impact limited to a few timeouts and increased tail latency; mitigations applied and stable. Follow-up owners: raj for infra/root cause DB, alex for runtime fallback and circuit-breaker implementation, cleo to coordinate feature-flag rollback and product comms.

cleo (product): I will pause the broadcast and revert flag rollout. Also will prepare customer comms draft.

raj (sre): I'll kick off a DB read replica spin (ticket INFRA-4321) and start query flamegraph for configstore.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATED • status: mitigated -> monitoring. responder: ingrid (oncall).

ingrid (oncall): Closing loop — will collect p95/p99 graphs, then schedule 1-hour postmortem with owners. Leaving the thread now; ping me for updates.

sarah (oncall): Great work team. Leaving handoff notes in the incident runbook. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: INCIDENT TRANSITIONED to postmortem queue at 2026-03-15T09:23:09Z
